tactical_description: Barcelona attempts to build from the back using a 3-2-5 structure, with the pivots dropping deep to draw out the Real Betis mid-block. Betis maintains a compact 4-4-2 defensive shape, focusing on closing the central passing lanes and forcing Barcelona into wide areas. Barcelona's center-backs look for vertical options but are met with disciplined horizontal shifting from the Betis midfield line.
key_tactical_insight: A compact mid-block effectively nullifies central progression when defensive spacing is maintained below 10-12 meters between lines.
coach_actionable_advice: Encourage double-pivots to alternate heights to create diagonal passing lanes and unbalance the opposition's first line of pressure.

tactical_description: Barcelona shifts the ball to the right flank, attempting to utilize Lamine Yamal's positioning in the half-space to drag the Betis left-back out of position. Real Betis responds by dropping into a low-block, with the wingers tracking back to provide double-coverage on the wings. Barcelona's circulation is too slow to bypass the organized defensive layers.
key_tactical_insight: Static wide possession allows the defense to regroup and establish numerical superiority in the box.
coach_actionable_advice: Implement third-man runs from the opposite half-space to exploit the focus of the defensive line on the ball-side.
suggested_training_drill: Final Third Overloads: 3v2 on the Flank

tactical_description: Real Betis capitalizes on a Barcelona turnover in the middle third. They quickly transition wide to the right. As the cross is delivered, Antony (7) makes a ghosting run from the blind side of the Barcelona left-back. Barcelona's center-backs are preoccupied with the central striker, leaving the far post completely exposed for the finish.
key_tactical_insight: Defensive transition failures often stem from a lack of weak-side tracking during rapid vertical attacks.
coach_actionable_advice: Full-backs must maintain a 'see-ball, see-man' body orientation when the opposition enters the final third from the opposite wing.

tactical_description: Barcelona executes an inswinging corner targeting the edge of the six-yard box. They attempt to block the Betis goalkeeper's path using two attackers. Betis employs a zonal-dominant marking system with three players in the 'high-traffic' zone, successfully clearing the first ball out of the danger area.
key_tactical_insight: Zonal marking in the six-yard box is superior for clearing direct deliveries when the defenders have height advantages.
coach_actionable_advice: Utilize 'short' corner variations to pull zonal defenders out of their designated blocks before delivering into the box.
suggested_training_drill: Attacking and Defending Set Pieces: Zonal vs Man-Marking
